chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

He said: A man said to another man, during the era of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), 'I had a wet dream involving your mother.' So it was raised to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). He said, 'This one has fabricated upon my mother.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what did he say to you?' He said, 'He claimed that he had a wet dream involving my mother.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him, 'With regard to justice, if I so desire, I would make him stand for you in the sun and whip his shadow, for the dream is like the shadow. But we shall whip him until he does not return to hurting the Muslims.' And in another report, he whipped him with a painful whipping.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: To have a wet dream / nocturnal emission

ai.seo_question: What was the judicial response of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to a man who accused another of a sexual dream involving his mother?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) mastery of legal analogy (qiyas) and wit, using the metaphor of the shadow to highlight the immaterial nature of the dream while prioritizing practical deterrence (uzr) over literal justice. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s ability to adapt judicial rulings to social contexts, balancing legal precision with mercy to preserve communal harmony. The incident underscores the principle that punishment serves not merely retribution but the prevention of future harm (darar) within the Muslim community.
